skill.name: cold-email-spam-lint
skill.description: Defines a cold email review workflow covering spam words, capitalization, emoji, clickbait, false threading, and link or image ratios. Deterministic execution requires a referenced Python scanner that is not included in this package.
skill.summary: Review cold email drafts using six documented checks and line-by-line flags, with an external scanner required for deterministic results.
skill.author: cmj-hub

security_audit.summary: All 15 static findings are false positives involving Markdown formatting, fixed repository references, or a source citation. Semantic review found unsafe shell interpolation of email text and conflicting score thresholds that could approve risky drafts. The referenced scanner and lexicon are absent, so implementation safety and claimed performance cannot be verified.

remediation.issue: Email text is interpolated into a Bash command without safe argument handling.
remediation.suggestion: Pass subject and body through a process API argument array without a shell, or read them from standard input. Test hostile text containing shell metacharacters.

remediation.issue: The risk score label conflicts with thresholds that approve high scores.
remediation.suggestion: Define whether higher scores mean greater risk or better quality, then align labels, weights, and verdict thresholds. Test clean and heavily flagged drafts.

remediation.issue: The scanner and reference files are not included in the reviewed package.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle required dependencies or declare an immutable companion package. Review its code before execution and verify paths resolve to those trusted files.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Shell Interpolation of Email Text
semantic_findings.description: The Bash example inserts subject and body into double-quoted command arguments. Shell substitutions or embedded quotes in untrusted drafts could execute commands if followed literally.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill explicitly directs shell execution and shows raw placeholders without escaping guidance. Exploitation depends on literal interpolation by the consuming agent.

semantic_findings.title: Conflicting Risk Score and Send Thresholds
semantic_findings.description: The document labels the score as deliverability risk but assigns 'Ship' to 90-100 and 'Do not send' below 60. This conflict can produce incorrect send recommendations.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The risk label and high-score approval are explicitly documented. The missing scanner prevents confirming which score direction its implementation uses.

content.user_title: Review Cold Email Drafts for Spam Signals
content.value_statement: Cold email drafts can contain misleading subjects, promotional wording, and excessive links. This skill defines six review checks and a structured report, with deterministic execution dependent on an external scanner.
actual_capabilities: Defines six weighted review axes for email subjects and bodies.
Documents checks for spam words, capitalization, subject emoji, clickbait, and false reply or forward prefixes.
Specifies link-count and image-to-text thresholds for business email review.
Provides a report format with axis scores and line-by-line flags.
Documents a Python command interface accepting subject, body, and output format arguments.
limitations: The referenced Python scanner and lexicon are absent, so deterministic results and claimed execution speed cannot be verified.
The risk score label conflicts with the documented send thresholds.
Content checks cannot guarantee inbox placement or assess sender authentication, reputation, or recipient consent.
The shell example requires safe argument handling before use with untrusted email text.

use_cases.title: Review Sales Outreach
use_cases.description: Identify promotional wording, excessive capitalization, and misleading reply prefixes before reviewing a sales draft for sending.

use_cases.title: Check Campaign Drafts
use_cases.description: Apply the same six documented checks across campaign drafts and collect line-level issues for editorial review.

use_cases.title: Check Partnership Emails
use_cases.description: Review partnership requests for clickbait, subject emoji, and unnecessary links before contacting potential partners.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this subject and body against the six documented spam checks: [subject] [body]. List flags without claiming scanner execution.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review without the external scanner.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Reply Prefix
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [subject] and [body]. There is no prior thread. Flag misleading reply prefixes, capitalization, subject emoji, and spam wording.
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review of a new outreach message.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Revisions
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these drafts: [original] [revision]. Report changes across all six checks. Do not invent scores or guarantee inbox placement.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Draft Batch
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [draft batch] with line-level flags. Execute only a verified scanner through shell-free arguments. Resolve score direction before assigning send verdicts.

output_examples.input: Subject: Re: URGENT pipeline update. Body: You will not believe this offer. No prior conversation exists.
output_examples.output: Subject flags: false reply prefix and spam-trigger wording. Body flag: clickbait wording. Deterministic score unavailable because the scanner is not included.

output_examples.input: Subject: ACT NOW. Body: Review our offer at https://example.com/a and https://example.com/b.
output: Subject: uppercase wording and the listed ACT NOW spam trigger.
Body: two links exceed the documented one-link threshold.
Send verdict withheld until score direction is clarified.

best_practices: Verify the scanner and reference files before execution, then pass email text without shell interpolation.
Clarify score direction and test clean and heavily flagged drafts before using send verdicts.
Review flags alongside sender authentication, reputation, and recipient consent.
anti_patterns: Paste untrusted subject or body text directly into the documented Bash command.
Treat a high score as approval without resolving the risk-label conflict.
Present heuristic review as verified scanner output or guaranteed inbox placement.

faq.question: What does this skill check?
faq.answer: It documents checks for spam wording, capitalization, subject emoji, clickbait, false threading, and link or image ratios.

faq.question: Is the deterministic scanner included?
faq.answer: No. The package contains the skill instructions but not the referenced Python scanner or lexicon.

faq.question: Does a higher score mean a safer draft?
faq.answer: The document is inconsistent. It calls the score a risk measure but approves high scores, so thresholds require clarification.

faq.question: Does this guarantee inbox placement?
faq.answer: No. Content checks cannot determine sender reputation, authentication status, recipient consent, or mailbox filtering decisions.

faq.question: Does the skill send email?
faq.answer: No sending operation is documented. The workflow reviews drafts and describes reports and send recommendations.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude or Codex?
faq.answer: The listing supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Deterministic execution additionally requires a verified scanner and a Python runtime.
